Gene Description

CASP8 encodes caspase-8, an aspartate-directed cysteine endopeptidase with tandem N-terminal death-effector domains. FADD-dependent recruitment organizes procaspase-8 in death-inducing and related cytosolic signaling complexes, promoting dimerization and context-dependent proteolytic processing. Its substrates include effector procaspases, BID, RIPK1 and gasdermin C: cleavage can initiate apoptosis, restrain RIPK-dependent necroptosis or promote inflammatory membrane damage in different cellular settings. CASP8 acts upstream of CASP3 in some GSDME-processing pathways, while the gasdermin supplies the pore-forming activity. Nonapoptotic functions include regulation of immune-cell activation, monocyte differentiation and phosphorylation-dependent migration. Human CASP8 deficiency causes combined defects in lymphocyte apoptosis and immune activation. Alternative products include catalytic-domain-deficient forms that can modulate death-receptor signaling; activity and localization therefore depend on product, complex and stimulus.

Core Functions

CASP8 performs limited proteolysis of signaling substrates. Effector-caspase maturation initiates apoptotic execution, while RIPK1 cleavage constrains necroptotic signaling; direct GSDMC cleavage provides a context-dependent route to gasdermin activation. These are substrate-dependent outputs of the same protease activity, not CASP8 pore formation.

Suggested Questions for Experts

Q: Should CASP8 gasdermin cleavage be represented as direct gasdermin protein maturation, as regulation of pyroptotic inflammatory response, or only in GO-CAMs where the input gasdermin is explicit?

Q: Which CASP8 immune-differentiation and developmental phenotypes should remain as flat GO biological-process annotations rather than being modeled through the more direct RIPK1/necroptosis checkpoint?

Q: Should catalysis-independent CASP8 migration signaling at lamellipodia receive a specific molecular-function term distinct from cysteine endopeptidase activity and death-effector-domain binding?

Q: What original donor experiment and historical source mapping produced the mouse Noc1p-Noc2p complex assertion transferred to human CASP8? The term permits non-yeast analogues, but the available donor citation has not resolved preribosomal-complex membership.

Q: Which original rat assays establish CASP8 death-receptor contact, cobalt/estradiol/ethanol/anesthetic responses and cell-body localization, and do their constructs and cellular contexts support transfer to human CASP8?

Q: What target experiment or corrected source mapping supports the CASP8 mechanical-stimulus annotation associated with the BAD prostate-cancer paper?

Q: Can the original tables and construct records resolve the remaining cross-species and isoform-qualified interaction assertions, especially mouse TRAF2/FADD/FLASH, the six neurodegeneration-network partners and the mutant-context FADD dataset?

Q: Which source experiment supports the precise syncytiotrophoblast/labyrinthine-layer differentiation assertion, including organism and the distinction between lineage differentiation and survival?

Q: How do the nine CASP8 products and cFLIP-dependent assemblies partition proteolytic activity, DED recruitment and nonapoptotic migration or immune signaling in human cells?

Suggested Experiments

Experiment: Introduce separation-of-function mutations into the CASP8 tandem DEDs in a CASP8-null human epithelial or lymphoid line, then quantify DISC recruitment, effector-caspase maturation, RIPK1 cleavage, and necroptosis after FASL, TRAIL, and TNF stimulation.

Hypothesis: CASP8 DED interfaces that recruit FADD and cFLIP differentially control extrinsic apoptosis versus RIPK1 cleavage.

Type: structure-function pathway assay

Experiment: Use cells expressing noncleavable endogenous GSDMC, GSDMD, or GSDME variants together with acute CASP8 rescue or inhibition to measure direct cleavage, pore formation, and cytokine release after DR6, TAK1/NLRP1, and TNF inputs.

Hypothesis: CASP8 directly determines which gasdermin substrate is matured in epithelial pyroptotic responses.

Type: gasdermin cleavage rescue assay

Notes

(CASP8-notes.md)

CASP8 notes

2026-09-30

  • Seeded and completed the human CASP8 review from GOA, UniProt, cached PubMed
    records, Reactome, GO-CAM models, and PAINT transfer context.
  • Kept the CASP8 core centered on three direct mechanisms: FADD/death-effector
    domain recruitment to death-inducing signaling complexes, Asp-directed
    cysteine endopeptidase activity that matures downstream procaspases and
    gasdermin substrates, and RIPK1 cleavage that restrains RIPK1/RIPK3-dependent
    necroptosis.
  • Tightened top-level GO:0006915 apoptotic process assertions toward
    death-domain receptor extrinsic apoptotic signaling, while leaving the
    abstract-only PMID:22891283 Fas vesicle row UNDECIDED.
  • Moved CASP8 away from effector-only GO:0097194 execution phase of apoptosis
    wording. CASP8 is an initiator that activates CASP3/CASP7 and other
    substrates by proteolytic maturation; CASP3 and CASP7 carry the direct
    executioner role.
  • Removed all 94 generic GO:0005515 protein binding rows. The FADD/CFLAR/FAS
    edges were either already represented by specific death-effector-domain or
    DISC annotations, and the BioPlex, binary-interactome, viral-inhibitor, and
    other screen edges did not identify a CASP8-specific molecular activity.
  • Removed the impossible Ensembl electronic GO:0030690 Noc1p-Noc2p complex
    mapping to human CASP8, together with stimulus-response and assay-readout rows
    that did not establish direct CASP8 work.
  • Kept pyroptosis, dectin-1 inflammasome, TLR3/TLR4 ripoptosome, N4BP1 innate
    immune, and host-pathogen perturbation rows as non-core where they captured
    real CASP8-containing complexes or substrate-cleavage branches.
  • Deferred rows whose visible cached evidence was abstract-only, review-derived,
    or centered on a different caspase or readout, including the
    HSP70/GATA1 localization rows, the COP/CARD-only protein paper, the
    CAAP/C9orf82 paper, the p23 paper, and specific immune differentiation terms
    sourced only to PMID:18309324.

2026-10-02 PR follow-up

  • Broad orthology and electronic angiogenesis, heart-development, animal-organ
    development, chordate-development, and neuron-apoptosis rows were kept non-core
    or marked over-annotated because they are transferred organismal contexts
    rather than direct human CASP8 biochemical activities.
  • Regulation-of-cytokine-production, lipopolysaccharide-response,
    innate-immune, and macrophage-differentiation rows were treated as
    inflammatory or differentiation contexts for CASP8 scaffolds and substrate
    cleavage, not as core death-receptor, DISC, or protease functions.
  • Generic immune-process, positive-signal-transduction, and cell-differentiation
    electronic rows were marked over-annotated because they are diffuse high-level
    projections, not specific steps carried out by CASP8.
  • Ensembl and rat-transfer Noc1p-Noc2p complex, cell body,
    protein-containing-complex-binding, cobalt, estradiol, ethanol, and anesthetic
    rows were removed as unsupported electronic projections rather than human
    CASP8 activities or locations.

2026-10-04 evidence and annotation reassessment

This entry supersedes the interpretation of the earlier notes where the two disagree. The older journal remains intact as provenance. The review retains all 264 source assertions, including every original reference, evidence code, qualifier and partner, and all nine UniProt product records. No new GO assertion is proposed. The important changes are scientific: supported generic interactions are retained, direct protease experiments are distinguished from downstream phenotypes, and unresolved evidence is no longer described as proof of absence.

Molecular work and compartment

CASP8 has two closely coupled molecular functions: aspartate-directed cysteine endopeptidase activity, and death-effector-domain recognition that organizes activation complexes. The catalytic synthesis combines substrate-dependent outcomes of the same enzyme: effector-caspase maturation, RIPK1 cleavage that restrains necroptosis, and direct GSDMC cleavage in the tested cancer-cell contexts. A separate DED unit captures physical recruitment and assembly. The previous three catalytic core entries have been consolidated without dropping their supported processes. Cytosol is accepted consistently as a central compartment; membrane, mitochondrial, cytoskeletal and nuclear pools are assessed in their particular contexts.

The canonical PMID:16916640 cache is abstract-only, but the author-hosted Stanford PDF supplied primary Results, the Figure 1 caption, kinetic comparisons and Methods. Recombinant DED-deleted CASP8 cleaves and activates human procaspase-7; activation-site mutants and subtraction of CASP8-alone reporter turnover constrain the result. The optimized buffers and engineered constructs are not measurements of endogenous DISC kinetics. The paper's CASP7 title therefore cannot justify discarding its CASP8 assays. The official GO:0008656 comment expressly includes active caspases that cleave inactive effector caspases. Proteolysis does not exclude that activator activity.

The GO-CAM index separately places CASP8 in cytosolic protein maturation and death-receptor pathways, consistent with these existing assertions. This index check is not a new model audit or a reason to invent additional annotations. In the GSDME sources, CASP8 is upstream of CASP3; CASP3 supplies the specific GSDME cleavage. In the GSDMC source, recombinant cleavage, cellular perturbation and a cleavage-resistant substrate support direct CASP8 action. Gasdermin supplies the pore, not CASP8 (PMID:32929201, PMID:33852854, PMID:35594856). The GSDMC correction concerns omitted funding acknowledgments, not altered experiments.

The former categorical exclusion of CASP8 from apoptotic execution was too strong. GO:0097194 permits other effectors in controlled cellular breakdown, and PMID:10891503 directly identifies plectin as a CASP8 substrate. Human-cell localization experiments distinguish active subunits from the prodomain, while recombinant plectin cleavage fragments include a rat construct; those observations are not interchangeable. CASP8 can perform a structural-substrate cut as well as activate downstream proteases. The ripoptosome study primarily establishes upstream complex/death regulation; its existing execution assertion is retained with curator deference and independent substrate support, not transformed into an exclusive terminal-executor claim (PMID:21737330).

Nonapoptotic and human disease evidence

The normal primary cache PMID:12353035 supplies direct human immunodeficiency context: "defects in their activation of T lymphocytes, B lymphocytes
and natural killer cells". It supports the existing T-, B- and NK-activation assertions that the old review left unresolved solely because the cited review was abstract-only. This clinical result does not identify every direct molecular step, nor equate CASP8 deficiency with classic ALPS. Only the complete abstract was available; no unseen patient-protein or rescue experiment is claimed.

Peripheral-blood monocyte differentiation involves CASP8 activation, downstream caspase processing and RIP1 cleavage that limits sustained NF-kappaB signaling. That is protease work, not merely an accompanying differentiation phenotype (PMID:17047155). Positive NF-kappaB signaling from prodomain-only CASP8 constructs is a different context and can coexist with this negative effect (PMID:12884866). The human-cDNA screen uses experimental expression evidence; IEP must not be called an electronic annotation (PMID:12761501). Its original CASP8 table remains uninspected, with independent target evidence supporting the retained direction.

The proteolytic-reporter study transfects CASP8 into human 293ET cells and measures a dose-dependent DEVDG reporter with a no-cleavage-motif control. Downstream caspases can contribute to the signal, but that does not invalidate the positive-regulation-of-proteolysis assertion (PMID:18387192). Human-cell migration experiments separately use catalytic-site and Y380 variants to distinguish protease activity from localization and migration signaling (PMID:18216014). No new migration molecular function or broad human developmental process is manufactured from these findings.

Interaction evidence and its limits

The former removal of all 94 generic binding rows on informativeness grounds is withdrawn. Source-specific reading supports qualified complex association, direct recognition in selected assays, or explicit uncertainty. Five existing rows are refined where the target experiment supports a narrower function: RIPK1 and NIK kinase binding by CASP8 prodomain constructs, nuclear androgen receptor binding, SHP1 phosphatase binding, and FADD DED binding. None makes CASP8 a kinase, receptor, phosphatase or ubiquitin ligase. The exact long-FLIP, Fas, UNG and FMR1 suffixes and the mouse/viral partner identifiers remain literal.

Several papers contain positive controls that their titles or abstracts obscure. These include CASP8 in apoptotic U937 receptor complexes despite receptor-independent monocyte differentiation, positive Jurkat DISC controls despite defective DU145 signaling, and CASP8 recruitment in sensitive human cells despite inhibitory complexes in resistant cells (PMID:17047155, PMID:14612908, PMID:18846110). FASLG capture establishes a ligand-containing receptor complex, not direct contact between an extracellular ligand and cytosolic CASP8. BCAP31 coimmunoprecipitation is retained even though its original in-vitro direct-binding experiment was negative; an unidentified bridge was proposed (PMID:9334338).

Where a source's exact assay or table is inaccessible but separately read evidence establishes the same literal partner interaction, retention explicitly names the independent support and defers to the experimental curator. That does not authenticate the uninspected original dataset. UniProt repeats many exact edges, but can share IntAct provenance and is not an independent experimental replication. Novel network pairs without independently verified target evidence remain uncertain. The mutant-context breast-cancer FADD record and unresolved mouse/viral construct mappings also retain their specific uncertainties rather than being generalized from ordinary human FADD binding.

PMID:21713032 distinguishes a CASP8-negative migratory MISC from an agonist-induced apoptotic DISC positive control. Its 2019 and 2023 corrections alter cell/construct descriptions, labels and image presentation and disclose missing original H9 S1C data; the corrected Figure 5C retains the DISC control. No raw-image reanalysis is claimed. The PMID:21988832 correction changes an author name; the PMID:19060883 corrigendum changes an author name and affiliations. Neither announces an interaction-dataset correction. These notices are reflected in the reference assessments.

Unresolved propagation and citation questions

The Noc1p-Noc2p term explicitly permits analogous complexes outside yeast, so its name does not make a human annotation impossible. An official mouse graph contains the donor experimental assertion, but the linked Nur77/apoptosis source does not resolve preribosomal-complex membership in the accessible evidence. The exact original donor experiment and historical source mapping remain unresolved. The old confident removal is replaced by uncertainty, without asserting a corrected citation or fabricating a sequence analysis.

Rat transfers for death-receptor binding, cobalt/estradiol/ethanol/anesthetic responses and cell-body localization need their individual assay provenance. General death-complex membership is not proof of direct receptor contact; generic cytoplasm is not proof of the more specific cell-body term. These access limits are not evidence that the annotations are false. The BAD-associated mechanical-stimulus citation likewise lacks a resolved target assay; its IEP evidence must not be dismissed as electronic. The specific placental differentiation assertion remains uncertain because species and developmental evidence could not be reconstructed from the accessible review. Broad developmental and neuronal assertions already supported by curated transfer are retained with explicit limits, not called false simply for breadth.

PAINT assertions represent ancestral-node judgments. Target inclusion among descendant evidence is legitimate, and donor-list size is not a proxy for quality. The ancestral nodes and alignments were not independently inspected; no target-specific residue loss or phylogenetic placement claim is made. This review proposes no additional processes, no new partner-derived functions, and no removal based only on title, organism name or absence of a keyword.

Access and validation provenance

All referenced cached abstracts and all 42 Reactome summaries were read by the author or the two bounded source consultants; selected full Methods, Results and captions were inspected where they resolve the target mechanism. Coverage is recorded per reference. A full_text_available flag is not a guarantee of a complete extracted paper: PMID:10521396 contains only a short abstract-like body, and several interactome HTML caches omit most original experimental text. External indexed or author-hosted passages are distinguished from unchanged canonical caches. Unseen images, supplements and target tables are not claimed as inspected.

One isolated standard research attempt used the installed Falcon provider and its normal fallback. Both failed without generating a report. The review therefore rests on the manually read sources and consultations; no provider report was authored or substituted. The earlier notes are historical statements, not evidence for the revised decisions. Long repeated YAML quotations and self-notes support have been replaced by source references and a small set of exact short anchors. The revised DRAFT status retains unresolved biological and access questions; warning counts are reported separately by normal validation.

The final process classification treats the tau proteolysis and upstream gasdermin-maturation-cascade assertions consistently with the broad catalytic core. Their substrate and causal limits remain explicit; acceptance does not turn the CASP3-mediated GSDME cut into direct CASP8 cleavage.

description: 'CASP8 encodes caspase-8, an aspartate-directed cysteine endopeptidase with tandem N-terminal
  death-effector domains. FADD-dependent recruitment organizes procaspase-8 in death-inducing and related
  cytosolic signaling complexes, promoting dimerization and context-dependent proteolytic processing.
  Its substrates include effector procaspases, BID, RIPK1 and gasdermin C: cleavage can initiate apoptosis,
  restrain RIPK-dependent necroptosis or promote inflammatory membrane damage in different cellular settings.
  CASP8 acts upstream of CASP3 in some GSDME-processing pathways, while the gasdermin supplies the pore-forming
  activity. Nonapoptotic functions include regulation of immune-cell activation, monocyte differentiation
  and phosphorylation-dependent migration. Human CASP8 deficiency causes combined defects in lymphocyte
  apoptosis and immune activation. Alternative products include catalytic-domain-deficient forms that
  can modulate death-receptor signaling; activity and localization therefore depend on product, complex
  and stimulus.'

  review:
    summary: Retain broad regulation of immune-system processes.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: Broadness does not make the ARBA inference biologically wrong. Human CASP8 deficiency impairs
      T-, B- and NK-cell activation, while inflammatory complexes use its protease and recruitment functions.
      These support this existing high-level regulatory assertion without making all immune outcomes independent
      core functions.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:12353035
    - reference_id: PMID:22267217

  review:
    summary: Refine broad peptidase activity to cysteine-type endopeptidase activity.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: CASP8 catalyzes internal peptide-bond cleavage after aspartate. Its measured proteolysis and
      curated specificity support the existing narrower endopeptidase term; the original donor/domain
      assertion remains intact. This refinement does not imply that the short catalytic-domain-deficient
      products retain enzymatic activity.
    supported_by:

  review:
    summary: CASP8 directly cleaves GSDMC.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: The human GSDMC substrate experiments combine recombinant cleavage, CASP8 perturbation and
      cleavage-resistant GSDMC. CASP6 also cleaves GSDMC in vitro, so the cellular CASP8 result does not
      establish unique enzyme specificity under all conditions. Gasdermin, rather than CASP8, forms the
      membrane pore.

      contact.

- id: PMID:21713032
  title: The naturally processed CD95L elicits a c-yes/calcium/PI3K-driven cell migration pathway.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Selected Results and Methods distinguish cl-CD95L-induced MISC, which lacks caspase-8,
      from the APO1-3-induced apoptotic DISC positive control that contains it in human H9 cells and activated
      peripheral lymphocytes. Retain the latter Fas association, not a role for CASP8 in the migratory
      MISC. The 2019 and 2023 corrections were read, including the corrected Figure 5C control caption;
      they are explicitly recorded below. Listed Fas isoform identity is preserved without a uniqueness
      claim. Corrections DOI10.1371/journal.pbio.3000521 and 3002027 alter cell/construct descriptions,
      labels and image presentation and disclose missing original H9 S1C data. Corrected Figure 5C retains
      the apoptotic DISC control; no raw-image reanalysis is claimed.
- id: PMID:21737330
  title: cIAPs block Ripoptosome formation, a RIP1/caspase-8 containing intracellular cell death complex
    differentially regulated by cFLIP isoforms.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Complete abstract and selected unique Methods, Results and Discussion read. Human keratinocyte
      cell-line and primary-cell experiments resolve RIP1/FADD/CASP8 complexes, IAP/cFLIP context and
      CASP8/RIP3-dependent death. Proposed complex-disassembly mechanisms and invariant native stoichiometry
      are not asserted as settled.
- id: PMID:21785459
  title: DJ-1 inhibits TRAIL-induced apoptosis by blocking pro-caspase-8 recruitment to FADD.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete cached and official publisher abstracts explicitly place competition between
      DJ-1 and procaspase-8 at the FADD death effector domain. This supports refinement of the FADD row
      to the already-existing GO:0035877 activity, with abstract-level access stated. The publisher full
      body remains subscription-only. The same abstract does not resolve the exact DR4 coassociation row;
      it cannot be rejected from the general TRAIL wording.
- id: PMID:21803845
  title: PMLRARα binds to Fas and suppresses Fas-mediated apoptosis through recruiting c-FLIP in vivo.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete abstract concerns PML-RARalpha effects on a Fas-associated complex and
      procaspase-8 exclusion in that perturbation. The exact positive/control Fas-CASP8 experiment could
      not be reconstructed; PMC and publisher body attempts failed. This original-assay uncertainty remains
      explicit while the generic Fas association is retained with independent target evidence. Context-specific
      exclusion is not a universal lack of Fas association or proof of miscitation.
- id: PMID:21980415
  title: Identification of a conserved anti-apoptotic protein that modulates the mitochondrial apoptosis
    pathway.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Complete abstract explicitly reports CASP8 and other caspase activation after CAAP perturbation
      in human cell lines. This establishes context, not unique causal responsibility of CASP8 for the
      phenotype; individual full activity controls were not independently re-read.
- id: PMID:21988832
  title: Toward an understanding of the protein interaction network of the human liver.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: The cached full body describes a liver protein-interaction network; the exact CASP8-FADD
      interaction-table row and its individual validation were not read. A keyword search is not a negative
      assay. The official 2017 correction concerns an author name only and does not establish an interaction-table
      defect. The generic FADD association is retained with independent same-partner support, while this
      dataset-specific assay remains unverified.
- id: PMID:22173242
  title: RIP1 is required for IAP inhibitor-mediated sensitization of childhood acute leukemia cells to
    chemotherapy-induced apoptosis.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete abstract explicitly identifies a RIP1-FADD-caspase-8 complex in childhood
      ALL cells after IAP inhibitor plus AraC treatment; RIP1 knockdown, kinase inhibition and TNF blockade
      suppress complex formation or interaction. Retain context-qualified association with each partner.
      Full Methods and direct-interface evidence were not read; do not generalize a co-complex result
      into a specific binary binding mode.
- id: PMID:22267217
  title: Dectin-1 is an extracellular pathogen sensor for the induction and processing of IL-1β via a
    noncanonical caspase-8 inflammasome.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete abstract explicitly describes recruitment of MALT1-caspase-8 and ASC to
      the CARD9-BCL10-MALT1 scaffold in dendritic-cell signaling. Retain qualified MALT1 association while
      deferring to the experimental curator. The abstract does not state the species or establish a mapped
      MALT1 domain interface; do not assign a CARD-domain interaction to CASP8 or infer direct MALT1-protease
      binding from membership alone.
- id: PMID:22274400
  title: 'Pick your poison: the Ripoptosome, a cell death platform regulating apoptosis and necroptosis.'
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete abstract both discusses the Ripoptosome and reports extensions involving
      cIAP, FLIP and RIP3 balance. It is not dismissed merely because it is review-like. Nevertheless,
      the exact CASP8-FADD and CASP8-RIPK1 physical assays were not accessible in the inspected material.
      The ontology citing this work for a complex definition is not a substitute for checking those source-specific
      pairs.
- id: PMID:22891283
  title: Vesicles released by activated T cells induce both Fas-mediated RIP-dependent apoptotic and Fas-independent
    nonapoptotic cell deaths.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: Complete abstract distinguishes FAS/RIP-dependent apoptotic and FAS-independent nonapoptotic
      responses to vesicles. Original CASP8-specific controls remain uninspected; the independent apoptotic
      function is retained without claiming all vesicle-induced death is CASP8 dependent.
- id: PMID:23955153
  title: Pathogen blocks host death receptor signalling by arginine GlcNAcylation of death domains.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete abstract supports bacterial NleB-mediated arginine GlcNAcylation and disruption
      of death-domain signaling. The actual CASP8 co-IP/control assays for FADD and RIPK1 were not inspected.
      This uncertainty concerns the original source-specific assays; the generic partner associations
      are retained using independently read same-partner evidence. Neither NleB enzymatic activity nor
      a direct death-domain interface is assigned to CASP8.
- id: PMID:24025841
  title: A type III effector antagonizes death receptor signalling during bacterial gut infection.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Selected Results and Methods use Fc-tagged Fas ligand and protein G to recover the Fas
      DISC from HeLa cells. This supports association of CASP8 with a ligand-containing receptor complex.
      It does not establish direct binding between the extracellular ligand and the intracellular protease.
      Retain qualified non-core association rather than inventing ligand-binding or receptor activity
      for CASP8.
- id: PMID:24438025
  title: Involvement of caspase 8 and c-FLIPL in the proangiogenic effects of the tumour necrosis factor-related
    apoptosis-inducing ligand (TRAIL).
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete abstract describes cFLIP expression, caspase-8 activation and angiogenic
      phenotypes in HUVECs. The physical CFLAR-CASP8 assay for the curated edge was not seen. Other primary
      sources establish this partner association, but they do not verify the original experiment here;
      no additional angiogenesis process assertion is proposed.
- id: PMID:25043603
  title: Apo2L/TRAIL and the death receptor 5 agonist antibody AMG 655 cooperate to promote receptor clustering
    and antitumor activity.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete abstract describes DR5 clustering by TRAIL plus AMG655 and enhanced apoptosis,
      but does not expose the CASP8-FADD interaction experiment. Preserve the experimental row while leaving
      its exact source-level assay uncertain. No claim of wrong receptor, wrong gene or absence of binding
      is justified.
- id: PMID:25890358
  title: TNFα sensitizes neuroblastoma cells to FasL-, cisplatin- and etoposide-induced cell death by
    NF-κB-mediated expression of Fas.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Selected Results, the relevant figure caption and Methods show Fc:hFasL-dependent recovery
      of FADD and caspase-8 from TNF-pretreated human SK-N-AS cells, with unstimulated or untreated comparisons.
      This supports ligand-containing DISC coassociation, not a purified FASLG-CASP8 binary interaction.
      Preserve the partner while qualifying the assay.
- id: PMID:25911380
  title: The seventh zinc finger motif of A20 is required for the suppression of TNF-α-induced apoptosis.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete abstract describes A20 ZnF7-dependent stabilization of cIAP1/2 in TNF signaling.
      It does not resolve the individual CASP8-FADD or CASP8-RIPK1 capture experiment. The full source
      was not read, so no negative verdict or inferred specific binding surface is justified.
- id: PMID:26942442
  title: An Evolution-Guided Analysis Reveals a Multi-Signaling Regulation of Fas by Tyrosine Phosphorylation
    and its Implication in Human Cancers.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Selected Results, the complete Figure 2 caption and Methods describe anti-Fas isolation
      of signaling complexes from human SW480 cells expressing wild-type or mutant Fas-V5, with caspase-8
      recruitment/processing and ligand-control comparisons. Retain Fas-complex association. Preserve
      P25445-1 exactly without claiming an isoform-exclusive biological interaction or a direct CASP8-Fas
      contact.
- id: PMID:30561431
  title: A protein-protein interaction map of the TNF-induced NF-κB signal transduction pathway.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: The primary Methods describe Virotrap using a human ORFeome FADD bait in HEK293T cells,
      TNF treatment, multiple irrelevant-bait controls and spectrum-based filtering. These methods make
      a physical-association dataset plausible, but the exact CASP8 prey row, scores and validation were
      not read. Do not present the generic method or a UniProt repeat as target-specific confirmation.
- id: PMID:31827280
  title: A dominant autoinflammatory disease caused by non-cleavable variants of RIPK1.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Complete primary abstract read. Human RIPK1 cleavage-resistant variants, patient blood-cell
      responses and mouse-model results are distinct; fibroblast compensation limits generalization. Supports
      CASP8 cleavage and necroptosis regulation, not a CASP8 disease-genetics association.
- id: PMID:32707033
  title: Kinase Interaction Network Expands Functional and Disease Roles of Human Kinases.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: The cached study is a kinase interaction network. The exact RIPK1-CASP8 AP-MS result,
      controls and table entry were not inspected; absence of a CASP8 main-text keyword does not contradict
      a supplementary result. Do not refine this row to protein kinase binding solely because the partner
      is a kinase.
- id: PMID:32814053
  title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread
    Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete abstract describes a modified yeast-two-hybrid interaction network. The
      six exact target pairs and isoform constructs were not retrieved from the primary table. UniProt
      repeats all six exact accessions, but those database records can share IntAct provenance and are
      not an independent experiment. Preserve RAF1, APP, UNG-2, PLK1, FMR1-7 and VPS33A separately; do
      not infer kinase binding, DNA repair, APP processing or RNA regulation from their names.
- id: PMID:32929201
  title: PD-L1-mediated gasdermin C expression switches apoptosis to pyroptosis in cancer cells and facilitates
    tumour necrosis.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Complete abstract and selected unique substrate-cleavage Results and Methods read. Human
      GSDMC, CASP8 perturbation, recombinant cleavage and cleavage-resistant GSDMC support direct proteolysis;
      CASP6 also cleaves in vitro. Official correction DOI10.1038/s41556-020-00599-1 concerns omitted
      funding acknowledgments, not altered figures or biology.
- id: PMID:33852854
  title: Gasdermin E permits interleukin-1 beta release in distinct sublytic and pyroptotic phases.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Complete abstract and selected unique human THP-1/mouse macrophage Results read. GSDME
      processing depends on its CASP3 cleavage site; CASP8 lies in the apoptotic cascade. No direct CASP8-to-GSDME
      substrate assignment or universal human/mouse equivalence is made.
- id: PMID:33961781
  title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: The normal cache marks full text available but its extracted HTML is only a short partial
      narrative. BioPlex AP-MS in 293T/HCT116 provides general study context; the exact DR4, CFLAR, Fas
      and FADD target edges, bait directions and controls were not read. This access limitation must remain
      explicit. Independent lower-throughput evidence for some partners does not authenticate these four
      dataset entries.
- id: PMID:34012073
  title: The metabolite α-KG induces GSDMC-dependent pyroptosis through death receptor 6-activated caspase-8.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Legacy cache contains extracted PDF text; complete abstract and opening body read. DR6-associated
      CASP8/GSDMC pathway is reported under metabolite perturbation. Individual full controls and every
      image were not inspected.
- id: PMID:34591612
  title: A protein interaction landscape of breast cancer.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: The cache full-text flag is true but the extracted HTML is short and incomplete. This
      breast-cancer interaction study includes genotype/context dependence; the exact CASP8-FADD edge
      and wild-type versus mutant bait provenance were not read. A generic FADD mechanism must not be
      presented as validation of this specific experimental construct.
- id: PMID:35446120
  title: Calmodulin Binding Activates Chromobacterium CopC Effector to ADP-Riboxanate Host Apoptotic Caspases.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Complete abstract read. CaM activates bacterial CopC, which modifies host apoptotic
      caspases including CASP8. CaM-binding and ADP-riboxanation activities belong to CopC; they are not
      transferred to CASP8.
- id: PMID:35594856
  title: Human NLRP1 is a sensor of pathogenic coronavirus 3CL proteases in lung epithelial cells.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Complete abstract and selected full Results/Figure 4 captions read. Human epithelial
      systems detect CASP8 processing and use caspase inhibitors; CASP3/GSDME genetic tests locate the
      gasdermin cleavage downstream. No CASP8 knockout or direct GSDME cleavage assay is claimed.
- id: PMID:38710704
  title: Deciphering DED assembly mechanisms in FADD-procaspase-8-cFLIP complexes regulating apoptosis.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Complete abstract and selected unique reconstitution, structural and cellular interface
      Results read. Human proteins include engineered FL-motif/catalytic/processing-site constructs; mouse
      iMEF and human HAP1/HeLa assays are distinguished. No complete-paper or raw image/supplement inspection
      claim, and no fixed native complex stoichiometry.
- id: PMID:8681376
  title: Involvement of MACH, a novel MORT1/FADD-interacting protease, in Fas/APO-1- and TNF receptor-induced

  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Complete primary abstract read. MACH/CASP8 cloning distinguishes active protease products

      competent.
- id: PMID:9184224
  title: FLICE is activated by association with the CD95 death-inducing signaling complex (DISC).
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Complete primary abstract read. FADD/DED recruitment, sequential DISC-associated processing
      and the cytosolic FLICE pool directly support the core mechanism; full original imaging/biochemical
      controls were not inspected.
- id: PMID:9208847
  title: Casper is a FADD- and caspase-related inducer of apoptosis.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete abstract explicitly states that Casper/CFLAR interacts with caspase-8 and
      summarizes CASP8 recruitment through the FADD DED. Both curated associations are retained with abstract-level
      access and curator deference. Distinct-domain wording for Casper does not identify the exact CASP8-binding
      surface in this excerpt. The specific FADD DED activity is covered by separately supported existing
      assertions; this reference does not establish an additional interface-specific annotation.
- id: PMID:9334338
  title: p28 Bap31, a Bcl-2/Bcl-XL- and procaspase-8-associated protein in the endoplasmic reticulum.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Selected full Methods/Results/Discussion describe tagged human BCAP31 and caspase-8
      coimmunoprecipitation, specificity comparisons including Bax, and BCAP31 cleavage. Crucially, the
      authors did not detect direct BCAP31-caspase-8 binding in vitro and proposed an unidentified bridging
      factor. Retain qualified coassociation; do not convert weak sequence resemblance or substrate cleavage
      into proof of direct DED binding. The direct-negative assay does not negate the cellular co-IP.
- id: PMID:9343261
  title: Bovine herpesvirus 4 BORFE2 protein inhibits Fas- and tumor necrosis factor receptor 1-induced
    apoptosis and contains death effector domains shared with other gamma-2 herpesviruses.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: UNVERIFIED
    review_notes: The complete official abstract explicitly reports yeast-two-hybrid binding of bovine-herpesvirus
      BORFE2 to the caspase-8 prodomain; FADD appears in the background mechanism. The primary PDF/construct
      details were not obtained. An official current Q1XBR6 accession-to-BORFE2 mapping was also not obtained,
      so the exact viral identifier and host construct remain unresolved. Preserve that uncertainty, not
      a wrong-species or wrong-gene allegation. The viral partner is not a normal human core function.
- id: PMID:9560245
  title: ARC, an inhibitor of apoptosis expressed in skeletal muscle and heart that interacts selectively
    with caspases.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Selected full Methods and Results show ARC/NOL3 co-IP with human CASP8, specificity
      comparisons against other caspases, and interaction with the CASP8 N-terminal 1-215 fragment but
      not residues 216-496; catalytic C377S and empty-vector controls constrain activity experiments.
      This supports qualified ARC association. CASP8 using its own DED-containing region does not imply
      that its partner supplies a DED, and the NOL3 CARD was not independently mapped as the binding surface
      here.

core_functions:
- description: CASP8 performs limited proteolysis of signaling substrates. Effector-caspase maturation
    initiates apoptotic execution, while RIPK1 cleavage constrains necroptotic signaling; direct GSDMC
    cleavage provides a context-dependent route to gasdermin activation. These are substrate-dependent
    outputs of the same protease activity, not CASP8 pore formation.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0004197
    label: cysteine-type endopeptidase activity
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0008625
    label: extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway via death domain receptors
  - id: GO:0060546
    label: negative regulation of necroptotic process
  - id: GO:0051604
    label: protein maturation
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005829
    label: cytosol
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:16916640
  - reference_id: PMID:31827280
    supporting_text: 'by caspase-8 separates the RIPK1 kinase domain from the

      intermediate and death domains.'
    reference_section_type: ABSTRACT
  - reference_id: PMID:32929201
    supporting_text: GSDMC is specifically cleaved by caspase-8 with TNFα treatment,
    reference_section_type: ABSTRACT
- description: CASP8 death-effector domains recognize FADD and related DED partners to build activation
    platforms and regulate procaspase recruitment. Structural reconstitutions and cellular interface tests
    support this interaction mechanism; engineered complex stoichiometries do not establish one invariant
    native assembly.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0035877
    label: death effector domain binding
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0071550
    label: death-inducing signaling complex assembly
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005829
    label: cytosol
  in_complex:
    id: GO:0031264
    label: death-inducing signaling complex
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:9184224
    supporting_text: 'FLICE binds to FADD through

      its N-terminal DED.'
    reference_section_type: ABSTRACT
  - reference_id: PMID:38710704
    supporting_text: 'assemble through death-effector domains

      (DEDs)'
    reference_section_type: ABSTRACT
proposed_new_terms: []
suggested_questions:
- question: Should CASP8 gasdermin cleavage be represented as direct gasdermin protein maturation, as
    regulation of pyroptotic inflammatory response, or only in GO-CAMs where the input gasdermin is explicit?
  experts: []
- question: Which CASP8 immune-differentiation and developmental phenotypes should remain as flat GO biological-process
    annotations rather than being modeled through the more direct RIPK1/necroptosis checkpoint?
  experts: []
- question: Should catalysis-independent CASP8 migration signaling at lamellipodia receive a specific
    molecular-function term distinct from cysteine endopeptidase activity and death-effector-domain binding?
  experts: []
- question: What original donor experiment and historical source mapping produced the mouse Noc1p-Noc2p
    complex assertion transferred to human CASP8? The term permits non-yeast analogues, but the available
    donor citation has not resolved preribosomal-complex membership.
- question: Which original rat assays establish CASP8 death-receptor contact, cobalt/estradiol/ethanol/anesthetic
    responses and cell-body localization, and do their constructs and cellular contexts support transfer
    to human CASP8?
- question: What target experiment or corrected source mapping supports the CASP8 mechanical-stimulus
    annotation associated with the BAD prostate-cancer paper?
- question: Can the original tables and construct records resolve the remaining cross-species and isoform-qualified
    interaction assertions, especially mouse TRAF2/FADD/FLASH, the six neurodegeneration-network partners
    and the mutant-context FADD dataset?
- question: Which source experiment supports the precise syncytiotrophoblast/labyrinthine-layer differentiation
    assertion, including organism and the distinction between lineage differentiation and survival?
- question: How do the nine CASP8 products and cFLIP-dependent assemblies partition proteolytic activity,
    DED recruitment and nonapoptotic migration or immune signaling in human cells?
suggested_experiments:
- hypothesis: CASP8 DED interfaces that recruit FADD and cFLIP differentially control extrinsic apoptosis
    versus RIPK1 cleavage.
  description: Introduce separation-of-function mutations into the CASP8 tandem DEDs in a CASP8-null human
    epithelial or lymphoid line, then quantify DISC recruitment, effector-caspase maturation, RIPK1 cleavage,
    and necroptosis after FASL, TRAIL, and TNF stimulation.
  experiment_type: structure-function pathway assay
- hypothesis: CASP8 directly determines which gasdermin substrate is matured in epithelial pyroptotic
    responses.
  description: Use cells expressing noncleavable endogenous GSDMC, GSDMD, or GSDME variants together with
    acute CASP8 rescue or inhibition to measure direct cleavage, pore formation, and cytokine release
    after DR6, TAK1/NLRP1, and TNF inputs.
  experiment_type: gasdermin cleavage rescue assay
